requirements.quote:
When an HTTP/2 connection is first established, new streams are
   created with an initial flow-control window size of 65,535 octets.
requirements.condition: When an HTTP/2 connection is first established and a new stream is created.
requirements.required_behavior: Initialize the stream flow-control window to 65,535 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect the initial flow-control window assigned to a newly created stream.

requirements.quote:
The connection flow-control window is also 65,535 octets.  Both
   endpoints can adjust the initial window size for new streams by
   including a value for SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE in the SETTINGS
   frame.  The connection flow-control window can only be changed using
   WINDOW_UPDATE frames.
requirements.condition: When an HTTP/2 connection is first established.
requirements.required_behavior: Initialize the connection flow-control window to 65,535 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect the connection-level flow-control window immediately after connection establishment.

requirements.quote:
The connection flow-control window is also 65,535 octets.  Both
   endpoints can adjust the initial window size for new streams by
   including a value for SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE in the SETTINGS
   frame.  The connection flow-control window can only be changed using
   WINDOW_UPDATE frames.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint wants to adjust the initial flow-control window size applied to new streams.
requirements.required_behavior: Use SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE in a SETTINGS frame to communicate the adjusted initial stream window size.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame traces and subsequently created stream windows can be checked for use of the advertised setting.

requirements.quote:
The connection flow-control window is also 65,535 octets.  Both
   endpoints can adjust the initial window size for new streams by
   including a value for SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE in the SETTINGS
   frame.  The connection flow-control window can only be changed using
   WINDOW_UPDATE frames.
requirements.condition: When changing the connection flow-control window.
requirements.required_behavior: Change the connection flow-control window only through WINDOW_UPDATE frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not change the connection flow-control window through SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE or any mechanism other than WINDOW_UPDATE frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject different frame types and observe whether only WINDOW_UPDATE changes the connection-level window.

requirements.quote:
Prior to receiving a SETTINGS frame that sets a value for
   SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, an endpoint can only use the default
   initial window size when sending flow-controlled frames.  Similarly,
   the connection flow-control window is set based on the default
   initial window size until a WINDOW_UPDATE frame is received.
requirements.condition: Before receiving a SETTINGS frame that sets SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the default initial stream window size when sending flow-controlled frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a non-default initial stream window size before receiving that setting.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send flow-controlled frames before any applicable SETTINGS value is received and inspect sender window accounting.

requirements.quote:
Prior to receiving a SETTINGS frame that sets a value for
   SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, an endpoint can only use the default
   initial window size when sending flow-controlled frames.  Similarly,
   the connection flow-control window is set based on the default
   initial window size until a WINDOW_UPDATE frame is received.
requirements.condition: Until a WINDOW_UPDATE frame is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the connection flow-control window based on the default initial window size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not change the connection flow-control window merely because a SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE value is received.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can compare connection-window accounting before and after SETTINGS and WINDOW_UPDATE frames.

requirements.quote:
In addition to changing the flow-control window for streams that are
   not yet active, a SETTINGS frame can alter the initial flow-control
   window size for streams with active flow-control windows (that is,
   streams in the "open" or "half-closed (remote)" state).  When the
   value of SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE changes, a receiver MUST adjust
   the size of all stream flow-control windows that it maintains by the
   difference between the new value and the old value.
requirements.condition: When SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE changes.
requirements.required_behavior: Adjust every maintained stream flow-control window by new_setting_value minus old_setting_value, including active windows for streams in the open or half-closed (remote) state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish streams in relevant states, change the setting, and verify the exact delta applied to every maintained stream window.

requirements.quote:
A change to SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE can cause the available
   space in a flow-control window to become negative.  A sender MUST
   track the negative flow-control window and MUST NOT send new flow-
   controlled frames until it receives WINDOW_UPDATE frames that cause
   the flow-control window to become positive.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE change makes a flow-control window negative.
requirements.required_behavior: Track the negative flow-control window value.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can reduce the setting below bytes already consumed and inspect the sender's resulting window accounting.

requirements.quote:
A change to SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE can cause the available
   space in a flow-control window to become negative.  A sender MUST
   track the negative flow-control window and MUST NOT send new flow-
   controlled frames until it receives WINDOW_UPDATE frames that cause
   the flow-control window to become positive.
requirements.condition: While the flow-control window is zero or negative after a SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE change.
requirements.required_behavior: Wait until WINDOW_UPDATE frames make the flow-control window positive before sending new flow-controlled frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send new flow-controlled frames while the window is non-positive.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can observe whether any new flow-controlled frame is emitted before WINDOW_UPDATE restores a positive window.

requirements.quote: A SETTINGS frame cannot alter the connection flow-control window.
requirements.condition: When processing any SETTINGS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave the connection flow-control window unchanged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not alter the connection flow-control window based on a SETTINGS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can process SETTINGS frames, including SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, and compare the connection window before and after.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST treat a change to SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE that
   causes any flow-control window to exceed the maximum size as a
   connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE change causes any flow-control window to exceed the maximum size.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the condition as a connection error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can choose stream-window state and a setting delta that exceeds the maximum, then inspect the connection-level error and code.

requirements.quote:
A receiver that wishes to use a smaller flow-control window than the
   current size can send a new SETTINGS frame.  However, the receiver
   MUST be prepared to receive data that exceeds this window size, since
   the sender might send data that exceeds the lower limit prior to
   processing the SETTINGS frame.
requirements.condition: After a receiver sends a SETTINGS frame lowering the stream flow-control window, before the sender has processed that frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Remain prepared to receive data exceeding the newly advertised lower window size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assume the sender has immediately adopted the lower limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send in-flight data valid under the prior limit after the receiver advertises a lower setting and observe whether it remains receivable.

requirements.quote:
After sending a SETTINGS frame that reduces the initial flow-control
   window size, a receiver MAY continue to process streams that exceed
   flow-control limits.  Allowing streams to continue does not allow the
   receiver to immediately reduce the space it reserves for flow-control
   windows.  Progress on these streams can also stall, since
   WINDOW_UPDATE frames are needed to allow the sender to resume
   sending.  The receiver MAY instead send a RST_STREAM with an error
   code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR for the affected streams.
requirements.condition: After sending a SETTINGS frame that reduces the initial flow-control window size, when an affected stream exceeds the new flow-control limit.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver may continue processing the affected stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can create a stream above the reduced limit and verify that continued processing is accepted as a permitted behavior.

requirements.quote:
After sending a SETTINGS frame that reduces the initial flow-control
   window size, a receiver MAY continue to process streams that exceed
   flow-control limits.  Allowing streams to continue does not allow the
   receiver to immediately reduce the space it reserves for flow-control
   windows.  Progress on these streams can also stall, since
   WINDOW_UPDATE frames are needed to allow the sender to resume
   sending.  The receiver MAY instead send a RST_STREAM with an error
   code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR for the affected streams.
requirements.condition: When the receiver allows streams exceeding a newly reduced flow-control limit to continue.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue reserving the flow-control-window space rather than immediately reducing that reservation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not immediately reduce the reserved flow-control-window space merely because the advertised initial window was reduced.
requirements.why_checkable: Resource accounting can be inspected after the setting reduction while over-limit streams continue.

requirements.quote:
After sending a SETTINGS frame that reduces the initial flow-control
   window size, a receiver MAY continue to process streams that exceed
   flow-control limits.  Allowing streams to continue does not allow the
   receiver to immediately reduce the space it reserves for flow-control
   windows.  Progress on these streams can also stall, since
   WINDOW_UPDATE frames are needed to allow the sender to resume
   sending.  The receiver MAY instead send a RST_STREAM with an error
   code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR for the affected streams.
requirements.condition: After reducing the initial flow-control window, when choosing not to continue an affected stream that exceeds the new limit.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver may send RST_STREAM for the affected stream.
requirements.error_behavior: If RST_STREAM is sent under this option, use error code FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exercise the reset option and inspect both the frame type and its error code.

requirements.quote:
The CONTINUATION frame (type=0x09) is used to continue a sequence of
   field block fragments (Section 4.3).  Any number of CONTINUATION
   frames can be sent, as long as the preceding frame is on the same
   stream and is a HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION frame without
   the END_HEADERS flag set.
requirements.condition: When sending a CONTINUATION frame in a field-block-fragment sequence.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure its preceding frame is on the same stream, is HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION, and does not have END_HEADERS set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a CONTINUATION frame after a frame on another stream, after another frame type, or after a frame with END_HEADERS set.
requirements.why_checkable: The immediately preceding frame's type, stream identifier, and END_HEADERS flag are directly observable in a frame sequence.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Length field as 24 bits and the Type field as 8 bits with value 0x09.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit width and fixed type value can be checked directly in serialized frame headers.

requirements.quote:
Unused Flags (5),
     END_HEADERS Flag (1),
     Unused Flags (2),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the flags octet of a CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Lay out the flags as five unused bits, one END_HEADERS bit, and two unused bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The eight flag bits can be inspected directly in the serialized frame header.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Stream Identifier (31),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the stream-identifier field of a CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use one reserved bit followed by a 31-bit Stream Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The 32-bit field layout can be checked directly in serialized frames.

requirements.quote:
Field Block Fragment (..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a CONTINUATION frame payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the payload as a variable-length Field Block Fragment.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser or serializer can be checked for treating the entire payload as the field-block fragment.

requirements.quote:
END_HEADERS (0x04):  When set, the END_HEADERS flag indicates that
      this frame ends a field block (Section 4.3).
requirements.condition: When the END_HEADERS flag with value 0x04 is set on a CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat that frame as ending the field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not expect further frames as part of that field block.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame sequence can be checked to ensure field-block assembly terminates when bit 0x04 is set.

requirements.quote:
If the END_HEADERS flag is not set, this frame MUST be followed by
      another CONTINUATION frame.  A receiver MUST treat the receipt of
      any other type of frame or a frame on a different stream as a
      connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a CONTINUATION frame does not have END_HEADERS set.
requirements.required_behavior: Follow it immediately with another CONTINUATION frame on the same stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interleave another frame type or a frame on a different stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The next frame's type and stream identifier can be compared with the preceding unfinished CONTINUATION sequence.

requirements.quote:
If the END_HEADERS flag is not set, this frame MUST be followed by
      another CONTINUATION frame.  A receiver MUST treat the receipt of
      any other type of frame or a frame on a different stream as a
      connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When, after a CONTINUATION frame without END_HEADERS, a receiver gets a frame of another type or a frame on a different stream.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject each prohibited next-frame variant and inspect the resulting connection error code.

requirements.quote:
CONTINUATION frames MUST be associated with a stream.  If a
   CONTINUATION frame is received with a Stream Identifier field of
   0x00, the recipient MUST respond with a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When sending or receiving a CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the frame with a nonzero stream identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use Stream Identifier 0x00 for a CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The Stream Identifier field is directly observable in every CONTINUATION frame.

requirements.quote:
CONTINUATION frames MUST be associated with a stream.  If a
   CONTINUATION frame is received with a Stream Identifier field of
   0x00, the recipient MUST respond with a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a CONTINUATION frame is received with Stream Identifier 0x00.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject a CONTINUATION frame on stream zero and inspect the connection-level error and code.

requirements.quote:
A CONTINUATION frame MUST be preceded by a HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE or
   CONTINUATION frame without the END_HEADERS flag set.  A recipient
   that observes violation of this rule MUST respond with a connection
   error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a CONTINUATION frame is sent or received.
requirements.required_behavior: Require the preceding frame to be HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION without END_HEADERS set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept a CONTINUATION frame without such a predecessor.
requirements.why_checkable: A receiver test can vary the immediately preceding frame type and flag state and observe acceptance.

requirements.quote:
A CONTINUATION frame MUST be preceded by a HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE or
   CONTINUATION frame without the END_HEADERS flag set.  A recipient
   that observes violation of this rule MUST respond with a connection
   error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a recipient observes a CONTINUATION frame not preceded by HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION without END_HEADERS set.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject invalid predecessor sequences and inspect the resulting connection error and code.

requirements.quote:
Error codes are 32-bit fields that are used in RST_STREAM and GOAWAY
   frames to convey the reasons for the stream or connection error.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an error-code field in RST_STREAM or GOAWAY.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the error code as a 32-bit field.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized RST_STREAM and GOAWAY error-code field width can be measured directly.

requirements.quote:
NO_ERROR (0x00):  The associated condition is not a result of an
      error.  For example, a GOAWAY might include this code to indicate
      graceful shutdown of a connection.
requirements.condition: When decoding error code 0x00.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret it as NO_ERROR, indicating that the associated condition is not the result of an error.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder's symbolic mapping and semantic classification for numeric value 0x00 can be tested.

requirements.quote:
PROTOCOL_ERROR (0x01):  The endpoint detected an unspecific protocol
      error.  This error is for use when a more specific error code is
      not available.
requirements.condition: When decoding error code 0x01.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret it as PROTOCOL_ERROR, representing an unspecific protocol error.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder's mapping for numeric value 0x01 can be tested directly.

requirements.quote:
INTERNAL_ERROR (0x02):  The endpoint encountered an unexpected
      internal error.
requirements.condition: When decoding error code 0x02.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret it as INTERNAL_ERROR, representing an unexpected internal error.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder's mapping for numeric value 0x02 can be tested directly.

requirements.quote:
FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR (0x03):  The endpoint detected that its peer
      violated the flow-control protocol.
requirements.condition: When decoding error code 0x03.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret it as FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, indicating that the peer violated the flow-control protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder's mapping for numeric value 0x03 can be tested directly.
